mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in the federal funds rate (measured as the change in FEDFUNDS over the prior 3 months) predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as monetary easing reduces discount rates and boosts equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns in periods of FEDFUNDS decline are not significantly higher than the baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in the unemployment rate (measured as the change in UNRATE over the prior 3 months) predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as improving labor market conditions signal stronger economic growth and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns in periods of UNRATE decline are not significantly higher than the baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5% (as measured by the current monthly value), it signals a restrictive monetary policy that compresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns in periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% are not significantly lower than the baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 2000 thousand units (as measured by the current monthly value), it signals weak consumer demand and economic contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns in periods when HOUST < 2000 are not significantly lower than the baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is rising and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) is rising simultaneously (measured as positive 3-month changes in both series), it signals an inflationary monetary policy cycle that suppresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns in periods of simultaneous FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL 3-month increases are not significantly lower than the baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) and employment (PAYEMS) both decline over the prior 3 months (measured as negative 3-month changes in both series), it signals a broad-based economic contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns in periods of simultaneous INDPRO and PAYEMS 3-month declines are not significantly lower than the baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime defined by GDP growth (GDPC1) exceeding 3% annually and housing starts (HOUST) above 2200 thousand units, the S&P 500 is expected to produce positive forward returns over the next 60 trading days, as the economy remains strong and corporate earnings growth accelerates.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns in the late-cycle expansion regime (GDPC1 annualized growth > 3% and HOUST > 2200) are not significantly higher than the baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a supply shock regime defined by industrial production (INDPRO) falling below 100 (index 2017=100) and declining at a rate exceeding 0.5% over the prior 3 months, the S&P 500 is expected to produce negative forward returns over the next 5 trading days, as supply chain disruptions and economic contraction rapidly depress equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns in the supply shock regime (INDPRO < 100 and INDPRO 3m change < -0.5%) are not significantly lower than the baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
